pr_title: Apiserver dedups owner references before creating/updating/patching objects
pr_body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/first-contribution.md#your-first-contribution and developer guide https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/development.md#development-guide
2. Please label this pull request according to what type of issue you are addressing, especially if this is a release targeted pull request. For reference on required PR/issue labels, read here:
https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-release/release.md#issuepr-kind-label
3. Ensure you have added or ran the appropriate tests for your PR: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-testing/testing.md
4. If you want *faster* PR reviews, read how: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews
5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
apiserver allows objects being created/updated with duplicate owner reference entries, which may lead to huge objects being created in the system.

As discussed in the previous SIG meeting (Nov 4th). The API server adds a warning header and dedups  without failing requests. Duplication is determined over the entire entry, not just the UID field.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #96065

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
~This doesn't resolve https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/96065#issuecomment-721339514. Today the [field manager](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ac996a37f65a8f11640808a883e9522832ed364f/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/create.go#L164) ignores any [preprocessing](staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/rest/create.go) the apiserver does before creating/updating an object. cc @apelisse @jennybuckley~ As discussed in the SIG meeting, the deduping happens before we write managed fields. 

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
Duplicate owner reference entries in create/update/patch requests now get deduplicated by the API server. The client sending the request now receives a warning header in the API response. Clients should stop sending requests with duplicate owner references. The API server may reject such requests as early as 1.24. 
```

/sig api-machinery
/assign @lavalamp @deads2k

issue_context.title: apiserver lacks validation for duplicate owner reference entries
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
apiserver allows objects being created/updated with duplicate owner reference entries, which may lead to huge objects being created in the system.
```
$ kubectl get configmaps child -oyaml
...
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: ConfigMap
    name: owner
    uid: f78b92c5-d24c-410e-9bda-ab298ffe7f7d
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: ConfigMap
    name: owner
    uid: f78b92c5-d24c-410e-9bda-ab298ffe7f7d
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: ConfigMap
    name: owner
    uid: f78b92c5-d24c-410e-9bda-ab298ffe7f7d
...
```

**What you expected to happen**:
The apiserver either rejects the request, or silently removes the duplicates. 

Rejecting the requests is going to break the clients that is doing this, plus people won't be able to write to the existing objects without fixing the owner references. I'm going to add a validation and see if it breaks any in-tree components in tests [UPDATE: #96069- I didn't find any in-tree controller doing this]. OTOH silently removing the duplicates seems to be a safer path. Comments and suggestions are welcome.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Run https://gist.github.com/roycaihw/e4990f45fae50dbd0a69d44842191ea5. The result is similar to:
```
owner: &ConfigMap{ObjectMeta:{owner  default  0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 702 0 2020-10-30 15:38:55 -0700 PDT <nil> <nil> map[] map[] [] []  []},Data:map[string]string{},BinaryData:map[string][]byte{},Immutable:nil,}
child: &ConfigMap{ObjectMeta:{child  default  d7c01603-8f9f-426d-9d6a-564c99118968 713 0 2020-10-30 15:38:55 -0700 PDT <nil> <nil> map[] map[] [{v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>} {v1 ConfigMap owner 0847a511-2e7b-4e20-9044-050a637f2320 <nil> <nil>}] []  []},Data:map[string]string{},BinaryData:map[string][]byte{},Immutable:nil,}
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:
The garbage collector is capable of clean up the duplicates for both [in-tree resources](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c0c0aa341f0a3311db69f92a67caed88c9e36eb1/pkg/controller/garbagecollector/patch.go#L44) and [custom resources](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c0c0aa341f0a3311db69f92a67caed88c9e36eb1/pkg/controller/garbagecollector/patch.go#L145). 

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): master HEAD

/sig api-machinery
cc @lavalamp @deads2k
comments:
Such requests will also cause the `managedFields` to be [cleared](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ac996a37f65a8f11640808a883e9522832ed364f/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/create.go#L164).
```
E1103 11:24:56.284054 3850496 fieldmanager.go:186] [SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields for /, Kind=: failed to convert new object (/v1, Kind=ConfigMap) to smd typed: .metadata.ownerReferences: duplicate entries for key [uid="2c0020f2-7d51-4d27-9101-a8cc1d7e1ee5"]
```

@apelisse @jennybuckley FYI

/cc @liggitt 
the sig is interested in knowing your opinion
/triage accepted
Added the issue to the SIG meeting agenda tomorrow as well.

> Such requests will also cause the managedFields to be cleared.

yeah, we assume that this is a "set" (which is the same assumption you're making), and I think that's right.

> apiserver allows objects being created/updated with duplicate owner reference entries, which may lead to huge objects being created in the system

Is the concern about malicious clients or naive clients that append duplicate owner references? Are there actual examples of the latter?

> we assume that this is a "set"

with `uid` as the key?

> Is the concern about malicious clients or naive clients that append duplicate owner references? Are there actual examples of the latter?

the latter. The one that I'm aware of: https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-lifecycle-manager/issues/1237

In the meeting earlier today, the SIG more or less decided to a) add a warning header and b) dedup without failing requests.

Deduping should be over the entire entry, not just the UID field.

review_comments:
Two behaviors regarding managedFields that surprised me, but may be expected. FYI @apelisse 
1. once an object has empty managedFields, the field manager won't write managedFields for future requests made by this client, even if those requests don't contain duplicate owner refs. 
2. without this PR, the field manager still succeeded to write `managedFields` for custom resources, even when duplicate owner ref existed in the request. Note that `"f:ownerReferences"` in the custom resource doesn't contain UIDs. 

with this PR, for built-in resource:
```
# 1. create with dup owner refs
managedFields: [{apiserver.test Update v1 2020-11-18 19:44:36 -0800 PST FieldsV1 {"f:metadata":{"f:ownerReferences":{".":{},"k:{\"uid\":\"03d3ba47-a815-46aa-84c7-70ee450b7761\"}":{".":{},"f:apiVersion":{},"f:kind":{},"f:name":{},"f:uid":{}}}}}}]
# 2. update with dup owner refs
managedFields: [{apiserver.test Update v1 2020-11-18 19:44:36 -0800 PST FieldsV1 {"f:metadata":{"f:ownerReferences":{".":{},"k:{\"uid\":\"03d3ba47-a815-46aa-84c7-70ee450b7761\"}":{".":{},"f:apiVersion":{},"f:kind":{},"f:name":{},"f:uid":{}}}}}}]
# 3. patch, append a dup owner ref
fieldmanager.go:186] [SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields for /, Kind=: failed to convert new object (/v1, Kind=ConfigMap) to smd typed: .metadata.ownerReferences: duplicate entries for key [uid="03d3ba47-a815-46aa-84c7-70ee450b7761"]
managedFields: []
# 4. update, append a different owner ref
managedFields: []
# 5. patch, append a different owner ref
managedFields: []
```
for custom resource (note the UID isn't written in the managed fields): 
```
# 1-5. repeat all the steps above, the managed fields always read like:
managedFields: [{apiserver.test Update cr.bar.com/v1 2020-11-18 19:44:36 -0800 PST FieldsV1 {"f:metadata":{"f:ownerReferences":{}}}}]
```
without this PR, the behavior of built-in resources will be:
```
# 1. create with dup owner refs
fieldmanager.go:186] [SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields for /, Kind=: failed to convert new object (/v1, Kind=ConfigMap) to smd typed: .metadata.ownerReferences: duplicate entries for key [uid="29b54e45-e089-4b12-bfd6-6ab63f20204a"]
managedFields: []
# 2-5. repeat all the remaining steps:
managedFields: []
```
and the behavior of custom resources won't change.
I didn't expect the managedFields to stay empty. Does this also happen on apply?

> 1. once an object has empty managedFields, the field manager won't write managedFields for future requests made by this client, even if those requests don't contain duplicate owner refs. 

That's because we don't track fields for objects that don't have managed fields, until they are server-side applied. That's to prevent existing objects from suddenly becoming bigger (because of the managed-fields) on existing clusters.
When we wipe, we could decide that we need to keep tracking (by setting an empty list rather than a nil value), but I'd say this is WAI.

> 2. without this PR, the field manager still succeeded to write `managedFields` for custom resources, even when duplicate owner ref existed in the request. Note that `"f:ownerReferences"` in the custom resource doesn't contain UIDs. 

it looks like ownerReferences is considered atomic for custom-resources. Can you look at the CRD and say if the ownerReference list is associative?

> but I'd say this is WAI.

Thanks for the explanation! That makes sense. 

> it looks like ownerReferences is considered atomic for custom-resources

IIUC the field manager uses the CRD schema to determine that. The [CRD used](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18099e1ef7283d9ab09c45c5a4a90e26fdce1161/test/integration/etcd/data.go#L593-L606) doesn't have schema. I also verified that API server doesn't insert the in-tree object meta schema into CRD. I think this is expected.

> The CRD used doesn't have schema.

We treat all lists as atomic for schema-less CRDs, all good! 👍
I think that comment is correct and makes sense! 👍
managed fields get updated in `applyPatch`. Currently a bad request can still wipe out managed fields.
interesting how you mention that at the exact same time that this happened: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/96688

Wouldn't it be enough to also dedup before apply?
Well... we'd have to dedup on the patchObj we decode into unstructured I think.

In general, I think Apply would still be broken of sorts until we make all the fields you equal on keys.
This could even solve both problems because at least for apply the request would be rejected on duplicate keys?
Correct me if I'm wrong @apelisse

Apply does the schema validation so there's no way you're going to be able to apply duplicated keys. If you apply a key that is already in the object, it's going to be merged with the applied key. And, unfortunately, if the object has duplicated keys, I don't know if it can be applied.

here I'm thinking of: 
- if a patch appends a duplicate owner ref, the managedFields update will fail

mutating admission is not involved. But I agree #96688 is also a problem
Yeah what I meant is, that we should make all fields in the ownerRef keys in the schema so we replicate the same behavior?

> Apply does the schema validation so there's no way you're going to be able to apply duplicated keys

That's good news. So the problem I was thinking of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96185#discussion_r526397606 only happens to the other patchers (json patch, json merge patch, SMP)
